title: Zephyrine and the Hollow
premise: Casper Ashgrove has kept the Hollow Gate sealed for three years, selling harmless charms in a city that outlawed magic, until the wards collapse on the night the stars go out. He discovers the gate was never his to keep alone: it was bound by a covenant between realms, and its other keeper — a star-born woman named Zephyrine — has been imprisoned inside the Hollow for those same three years. To restore the covenant and bring back the stars, Casper must break her out, unmask the magistrate who engineered the blackout to hoard magic for himself, and choose between sealing the gate forever or reopening it at the cost of his own borrowed power. In the end, Casper sacrifices his magic to free Zephyrine, who rekindles the stars from within the Hollow, leaving both realms changed and the gate guarded by two keepers instead of one.
about_author: Petra Thackeray is a former archivist from the northern coast who writes fantasy about doors, borders, and the people paid to watch them. Her short fiction has appeared in several small-press anthologies; this is her first novel.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. On an ordinary market evening, Casper sells a luck-charm to a nervous young clerk, then watches every star above Grayhallow vanish at once as the border wards shatter like glass. The emotional beat is dread disguised as routine — he knows exactly what the falling wards mean, because he's been hiding what he is.

chapters.title: Charms for a Lawless City
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, three years earlier woven through present panic. Flashbacks reveal how he inherited the gatekeeper's post from his dying mentor and chose to hide rather than hold it. He packs to flee, but finds his mentor's old covenant-ring burning cold on his hand. Beat: guilt surfacing after long denial.

chapters.title: What Fell Through
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Something crosses the broken wards: a hollow-eyed wraith that speaks with his mentor's voice, demanding the ring. Casper barely escapes into the undercity, realizing the Hollow — the dead realm behind the gate — is leaking. Beat: terror sharpening into reluctant responsibility.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Lantern
chapters.summary: Introduce Magistrate Corvane Hale via his own POV. Hale addresses a frightened city, promising protection while secretly harvesting the fallen ward-magic into a private lantern. We learn he orchestrated the blackout. Beat: cold ambition; the reader sees the villain's tidy logic.

chapters.title: A Thief Named Wren
chapters.summary: New POV: Wren, a smuggler who deals in outlawed charms, catches Casper breaking into her cache of gate-keys. Instead of turning him in, she recognizes the covenant-ring — her grandmother was a keeper too. Beat: wary alliance formed over shared illegal inheritance.

chapters.title: Voices in the Hollow
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. At the cracked gate, he hears a voice singing through the stone — Zephyrine, the second keeper, sealed inside when the wards fell. She tells him the covenant requires two voices spoken together, and that Hale's lantern is drinking the magic meant to sustain her. Beat: hope with a deadline.

chapters.title: The Price of Small Magic
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The city cracks down; charm-sellers are arrested in sweeps. Wren's brother is taken, forcing her to choose between lying low and helping Casper reach the archive where the original covenant is written. Beat: personal stakes ignite the political ones.

chapters.title: The Archive Beneath the Bells
chapters.summary: Casper and Wren infiltrate the bell-tower archive and find the covenant text: the gate was shut not to imprison the Hollow, but to imprison something inside it — and Zephyrine went in willingly to contain it. Beat: the mission's moral simplicity collapses.

chapters.title: Zephyrine
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, inside the Hollow. Starved of starlight, she remembers the night she crossed over: the devouring thing called the Unlit, her bargain, her willing cage. She feels Casper listening and dares, for the first time in three years, to hope. Beat: loneliness answered.

chapters.title: Hale's Offer
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Hale captures Wren and offers Casper a deal: the ring and his silence in exchange for Wren's freedom and a place at Hale's side. Casper sees the lantern up close — full of stolen ward-light, enough to reforge the covenant or to rule. Beat: temptation wearing a reasonable face.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper refuses, burns his cover, and escapes with Wren during a wraith surge Hale deliberately unleashes to justify martial law. The city turns on its magic-touched. Beat: crossing the point of no return; justice must now come from outside the law.

chapters.title: The Undercity Rises
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Smugglers, charm-sellers, and the disenfranchised organize beneath the streets. Wren becomes their reluctant general, trading on every favor she ever banked. Casper teaches them the old keeping-rites. Beat: community forged from outlaws.

chapters.title: What the Ring Remembers
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The covenant-ring shows him visions: every keeper before him, including Zephyrine's sacrifice, and the truth that the ring feeds on the wearer's own magic. Using it will burn him out. Beat: acceptance of a price he can't yet name.

chapters.title: Storming the Lantern Tower
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV rotation (Wren, then Casper). The undercity assaults Hale's tower while wraiths pour through the failing wards. Wren frees the prisoners; Casper reaches the lantern chamber and finds Hale already pouring its light into himself. Beat: chaos, courage, near-defeat.

chapters.title: The Man Who Ate the Sky
chapters.summary: Casper vs. Hale. Hale, half-transfigured by stolen starlight, offers again — godhood shared. Casper shatters the lantern instead, releasing the light back toward the gate, and is nearly killed. Beat: power refused at terrible cost.

chapters.title: Into the Hollow
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Dying of ring-burn, he opens the gate and steps through to reach Zephyrine, leaving Wren to hold the city side. Inside: a beautiful, starving dark where the Unlit wears the faces of everyone he's failed. Beat: descent, surrender, love as compass.

chapters.title: The Second Keeper
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. She finds Casper and shields him from the Unlit, revealing the final clause of the covenant: it can be reforged only by a keeper giving up their magic entirely. They argue over who pays. Beat: two self-sacrificers learning to accept help.

chapters.title: The Unlit Speaks
chapters.summary: Shared POV. The Unlit reveals itself as the accumulated abandoned magic of both realms — every spell renounced, every gift outlawed, given nowhere to go. It doesn't want destruction; it wants a home. Beat: the monster reframed as consequence.

chapters.title: A New Covenant
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Instead of banishing the Unlit, they rewrite the covenant: the gate opens a controlled channel so renounced magic can return to the sky. Casper gives up his last spark to seal it, and Zephyrine kindles the returned light back into stars. Beat: climax — sacrifice transmuted into restoration.

chapters.title: Stars Over Grayhallow
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. From the tower ruins, Wren and the undercity watch the stars reignite as Hale falls, undone by the light leaving him. The crowd that hunted charm-sellers weeks ago now cheers them. Beat: catharsis; the law bends toward justice.

chapters.title: Two Keepers
chapters.summary: Casper and Zephyrine's alternating POV. Powerless but alive, Casper walks out of the Hollow hand in hand with Zephyrine, who must learn a world without her divinity. They take joint guardianship of the now-open, tended gate. Beat: quiet wonder, identity rebuilt from scratch.

chapters.title: The Gate That Stays Open
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Wren's POV, one year later. Grayhallow licenses small magics; Wren runs a legal shop beside the gate; the Unlit hums contentedly beyond the wards. Casper and Zephyrine teach new keepers. Final beat: power held in common, justice made ordinary, a door left open on purpose.
